requirements.title: Catalog plans cannot pass vacuously

source.excerpt:
All requirement, criterion, verification and plan IDs MUST be unique across the
catalog. Stable identities are independent of file placement. A requirement has
exactly one normative inline statement or exact tracked source, explicit supported
configuration applicability and observable criteria. Empty criteria remain
incomplete. Definitions may be reused; every criterion/configuration/required-stage
combination needs exactly one all-members plan. Empty/ambiguous/missing plans,
dangling links and unknown configurations cannot qualify.

requirements.rationale: An empty inventory is not successful coverage; one green unit member is insufficient when a consumer member is missing.

criteria.expected: Empty criteria or member lists produce findings; every selected member and stage requires current execution; unsupported case assurance remains unverified.

requirements.title: Mapping reviews bind their actual inputs

source.excerpt:
Mapping subjects include requirement identity, normative owner, origin/rationale,
applicability, criterion, plan/stage/configuration, relationships, full assertion
and declared input references, suite/command and testing/quality/assurance policy.
They exclude the review itself and unrelated implementation bytes. An input list
does not prove dependency completeness; unknown/shared changes broaden semantic
review. Mechanical binding MUST NOT write a passed review.

requirements.rationale: A filtered command or duplicate excerpt cannot keep an earlier review current.

criteria.expected: Stage, configuration, assertions, helper membership, criteria, source and command changes invalidate review; ambiguous source excerpts cannot bind current assertions.

requirements.title: Manual observation identity and age matter

source.excerpt:
Suite assurance establishes canonical command execution, not named-case selection.
Unsupported selected case-level assurance remains unverified. There is no required
JUnit adapter. Manual observation is a separate attributed current-change record
with exact plan subject, method context, actual result, observer, reference and
bounded age. It cannot qualify another source/stage. Future, stale, absent and
ambiguous observations fail closed; known contradictions remain visible.

requirements.rationale: Test the inclusive age boundary, one second beyond it, a future observation and a changed plan subject.

criteria.expected: Manual observations need the current subject, attribution and bounded age; future, expired or wrongly bound observations cannot pass.

requirements.title: Catalog changes bind a real provider baseline
requirements.rationale: A tree ID is not a baseline commit; duplicate manual members and a changed provider base cannot silently qualify.

criteria.expected: A catalog selection binds actual candidate and baseline identities, a real commit and valid unique manual members; observed provider baseline drift is rejected.

requirements.title: Catalog and policy inspection do not write Git metadata

source.excerpt:
Staged inspection MUST NOT acquire an index lock, write tree objects or lazily
fetch missing objects. It reads native `ls-files --stage -z` entries and hashes
the Git tree representation using `hash-object -t tree --stdin` without `-w`.
The exposed tree identity remains the exact Git object ID, not a new digest
format; inspection does not promise that the tree object has been materialized.
Unmerged entries, missing file blobs and unsupported modes fail closed. Gitlinks
outside the catalog may name commits available only in their submodule. The
whole staged inventory is bounded to 64 MiB and paths to 128 components. This
same reader serves selected organization-policy inspection.

requirements.rationale: Inspection must work without index/object write authority while retaining native Git identity and fail-closed missing-object handling.

criteria.expected: Requirements and selected policy reads preserve the index, object inventory and existing lock; identity matches Git for SHA-1/SHA-256, ordering, executable/symlink/gitlink modes and intent-to-add exclusions; missing file objects fail closed. Older Git with promisor configuration is rejected before object reads without modifying configuration.

members.assertion: Exact native Git tree equality across both object formats and modes with an untouched existing lock; missing blob rejected.
members.discriminating_case: An implementation using write-tree fails with the preexisting lock; including intent-to-add changes the expected tree.

members.assertion: Index bytes, owned lock bytes and complete object-file inventory unchanged, followed by exact write-tree equality.
members.discriminating_case: A new staged file invalidates the cached tree, so a hidden write-tree call cannot succeed under the existing lock.

members.assertion: Selected policy resolves under an existing index lock, leaves bytes intact and preserves Git tree identity.
members.discriminating_case: Even a semantically unchanged policy must not require writes to inspect its staged definition.

members.assertion: Legacy-Git safety preflight accepts a complete repository but rejects promisor configuration without changing its bytes.
members.discriminating_case: A Git version silently ignoring GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH must not fall through to object reads in a partial clone.

review.rationale: Reviewed current lock/object preservation and exact-tree tests plus the new legacy-Git configuration guard: complete repositories are accepted, promisor configuration is refused before object reads, and configuration bytes remain intact. Git subprocesses disable lazy fetch, transports and optional writes; the whole-file bindings include those inputs. Earlier live follow-ups exercised the pre-guard candidate and are not silently rebound as current-source execution.
